title: Seek the favour of the one God
source_text: Ἕνα οὖν τὸν ἐπὶ πᾶσι θεὸν ἡμῖν ἐξευμενιστέον καὶ τοῦτον ἵλεω εὐκτέον, ἐξευμενιζόμενον εὐσεβείᾳ καὶ πάσῃ ἀρετῇ. εἰ δὲ καὶ ἄλλους τινὰς βούλεται μετὰ τὸν ἐπὶ πᾶσιν ἐξευμενίζεσθαι θεὸν, κατανοησάτω ὅτι ὥσπερ τῷ κινουμένῳ σώματι ἀκολουθεῖ ἡ τῆς σκιᾶς αὐτοῦ κίνησις, τὸν αὐτὸν τρόπον τῷ ἐξευμενίζεσθαι τὸν ἐπὶ πᾶσι θεὸν ἕπεται εὐμενεῖς ἔχειν πάντας τοὺς ἐκείνου φίλους ἀγγέλους καὶ ψυχὰς καὶ πνεύματα. συναίσθονται γὰρ τῶν ἀξίων τοῦ παρὰ τοῦ θεοῦ εὐμενισμοῦ, καὶ οὐ μόνον καὶ αὐτοὶ εὐμενεῖς τοῖς ἀξίοις γίνονται ἀλλὰ καὶ συμπράττουσι τοῖς βουλομένοις τὸν ἐπὶ πᾶσι θεὸν θεραπεύειν καὶ ἐξευμενίζονται καὶ συνεύχονται καὶ συναξιοῦσιν· ὥστε τολμᾶν ἡμᾶς λέγειν ὅτι ἀνθρώποις μετὰ προαιρέσεως προτιθεμένοις τὰ κρείττονα εὐχομένοις τῷ θεῷ μυρίαι ὅσαι ἄκλητοι συνεύχονται δυνάμεις ἱεραὶ, συμπαρέχουσαι τῷ ἐπικήρῳ ἡμῶν γένει καὶ, ἵν᾿ οὕτως εἴπω, συναγωνιῶσαι δι᾿ οὓς ὁρῶσιν ἀντιστρατευο μένους καὶ ἀνταγωνιζομένους δαίμονας τῇ σωτηρίᾳ μάλιστα τῶν ἑαυτοὺς ἀνατιθέντων θεῷ καὶ μὴ φροντιζόντων τῆς τῶν δαιμόνων ἔχθρας, ἐὰν ἐκεῖνοι ἐξαγριαίνωσι πρὸς τὸν ἄνθρωπον, φεύγοντα μὲν αὐτῶν τὰς διὰ κνίσσης καὶ αἵματος θεραπείας παντὶ δὲ τρόπῳ λόγων καὶ πράξεων σπεύδοντα οἰκειοῦσθαι καὶ ἑνοῦσθαι τῷ ἐπὶ πᾶσι θεῷ διὰ τοῦ καταλύσαντος μυρίους δαίμονας Ἰησοῦ, ἡνίκα περιῄει „ἰώμενος“ καὶ ἐπιστρέφων „τοὺς καταδυναστευομένους ὑπὸ τοῦ διαβόλου.“
pass_a_gloss: The one God over all, therefore, must be propitiated by us and must be prayed to (εὐκτέον) to be gracious (ἵλεως), propitiated by piety (εὐσέβεια) and every virtue (ἀρετή). And if he wants to propitiate also some others after (μετά) the God over all, let him consider (κατανοέω) that, just as the movement (κίνησις) of its shadow (σκιά) follows (ἀκολουθέω) the moving body, in the same way, to propitiating the God over all there follows (ἕπομαι) having well-disposed (εὐμενεῖς) all His friends (φίλοι), angels (ἄγγελοι) and souls (ψυχαί) and spirits (πνεύματα). For they perceive those worthy (ἄξιοι) of the favour (εὐμενισμός) from God, and not only do they themselves become well disposed to the worthy, but also work with (συμπράττω) those wishing to serve (θεραπεύω) the God over all, and propitiate and pray with (συνεύχομαι) and join in asking (συναξιόω); so that we dare (τολμάω) to say that with men who with deliberate choice (προαίρεσις) set before themselves (προτίθεμαι) the better things, praying to God, countless (μυρίαι ὅσαι) uncalled (ἄκλητοι) holy powers pray together, aiding together (συμπαρέχω) our mortal (ἐπίκηρος) race (γένος) and, so to say, sharing the struggle (συναγωνιάω), on account of the demons they see warring against and contending against (ἀνταγωνίζομαι) the salvation (σωτηρία) especially of those dedicating (ἀνατίθημι) themselves to God and not caring for (φροντίζω) the enmity (ἔχθρα) of the demons, if they grow savage (ἐξαγριαίνω) toward the man fleeing (φεύγω) their services through savour and blood and in every manner of words and actions hastening (σπεύδω) to be made kin (οἰκειόομαι) and united (ἑνόομαι) to the God over all through Jesus, who destroyed (καταλύω) countless demons when he went about (περιέρχομαι) 'healing' (ἰάομαι) and turning (ἐπιστρέφω) 'those oppressed by the devil (διάβολος)'.
pass_b_english: So it is the one God over all whose favour we must seek, and we must pray to Him to be gracious; His favour is won by piety and by every virtue. But if Celsus wants us to win the favour of some others too, after the God over all, let him consider this: just as the movement of its shadow follows a body in motion, in the same way, winning the favour of the God over all brings with it the goodwill of all His friends, angels and souls and spirits.

For they perceive who are worthy of favour from God, and not only do they themselves become well disposed to the worthy, but they also work together with those who wish to serve the God over all; they seek His favour for them, they pray with them and join in their requests. So we dare to say that when men who by deliberate choice set the better things before them pray to God, countless holy powers pray with them unbidden. They stand by our mortal race and, if I may put it so, share its struggle and anguish, because they see the demons waging war and contending against salvation, most of all the salvation of those who dedicate themselves to God and take no thought of the hatred of the demons, if the demons grow savage against the man who flees their worship with the smoke of sacrifice and blood, and who by every manner of word and deed hastens to be made kin to the God over all and united with Him through Jesus, who overthrew countless demons when He went about “healing” and turning back “those who were oppressed by the devil” (Acts 10:38).

choices.choice: Acts 10:38 reads διῆλθεν εὐεργετῶν καὶ ἰώμενος πάντας τοὺς καταδυναστευομένους ὑπὸ τοῦ διαβόλου; Origen quotes ‘healing’ and ‘those oppressed by the devil’ within his own sentence and adds ἐπιστρέφων (‘turning back’), which is his, not Luke’s; the quotation marks enclose only the Lukan words. Origen’s quoted phrase lacks πάντας, so the English follows Origen (‘those who were oppressed by the devil’), not Acts (‘all who were oppressed’). βούλεται has no expressed subject; ‘Celsus’ is supplied from 8.63 (he urged winning the favour of rulers), and ‘us’ after ‘wants’ is supplied from the sense. ἐξευμενίζονται (middle) in the list of the angels’ acts is rendered ‘they seek His favour for them’. συναγωνιῶσαι rendered ‘share its struggle and anguish’ (Origen marks the word with ἵν᾿ οὕτως εἴπω, ‘if I may put it so’). The ἐάν clause (ἐὰν ἐκεῖνοι ἐξαγριαίνωσι ...) depends on μὴ φροντιζόντων (‘take no thought of the demons’ hatred, if they grow savage’); the draft’s separate sentence ‘This is so even if’ attached it to the whole and turned ‘if’ into ‘even if’, so review folded it back into the sentence and the third paragraph into the second. The angels praying with the faithful is not tied to a single verse here, so no further citation.

ἕπεται εὐμενεῖς ἔχειν: dropped added 'to us'; 'winning the favour of the God over all brings with it the goodwill of all His friends'
ἵλεω εὐκτέον 'we must pray to Him to be gracious'
